problems.source_says: The paper states neither the unit nor a per-arm n, and its wording does not settle it: it writes 'participants in the group-AI condition' for a per-pair mean (4.35 = 209 prompts / 48). The printed SEs and df fit 48 team-level units in each pair arm and 96 people in individual-AI. Figure 5 total-effect SEs computed from the Section 3.1 SDs: G-AI vs G 0.067, 0.084, 0.948 with 48 per arm, printed 0.07, 0.08, 0.96 (96 per arm gives 0.048, 0.060, 0.671); G-AI vs I-AI 0.072, 0.088, 0.825 with 48 + 96, printed 0.07, 0.09, 0.83 (96 + 96 gives 0.057, 0.072, 0.719). The t(142) tests fit the same split (high-quality AI uptake rate 10.25 vs printed 10.23, against 12.33 with 96 + 96; broad generative strategy 2.93 vs printed 2.95, against 3.75), as do the a-path SEs 0.05 and 0.20; only the DAHI a-path SE (0.36) fits neither count. So the pair-arm creativity scores behind the arm SDs and the Figure 5 totals are per team, 48 per arm. This is arithmetic on printed numbers, not a statement of the paper. The form flags the unit as unconfirmed (open_questions; reconciliation confirmed false) but keeps 'participant' and an implied n of 96. A standard error built with n = 96 per pair arm would be 29 percent too small. The people count of 96 is unaffected.

problems.form_value: Exclusions: 'The paper does not say whether the exclusions came before or after pairing and assignment, or what happened to the excluded people's partners.' Summary: '96 university students (100 recruited, 4 excluded) were randomly paired'
problems.source_says: The text implies the exclusions came after random pairing. On arrival, participants were randomly paired, then given the standardized instructions, then took a pre-task questionnaire, then were assigned and did the creativity task (pp. 7-8). The 4 were excluded for failing to follow task instructions (p. 7), so they had already been paired. On the paper's own accounting (100 recruited, only these 4 lost), 100 people (50 pairs) were randomly paired, not the 96 analyzed. Because the 96 form 48 complete pairs (F(1, 47), p. 17), the 4 excluded would have been 2 whole pairs. This is a reading of the procedure: the paper prints no count at pairing or assignment, so n_randomized null stays right. No count or verdict changes.

One study only, and the paper names no other paper that uses these participants, so a blank sample_overlap is right on the document. The JCAL 2026 article is a later version of the same paper with the same 96 students, not a second sample.

summary: The people counts hold: 100 recruited, 4 excluded, and 96 university students analyzed, each in all three conditions, so this single randomized within-subject study clears the 50-person bar on its own (pp. 7-8). The coding is still refuted on detail: the form treats the creativity outcomes as participant-level with 96 per arm, while the printed df and SEs (t(142), F(1, 47), Figure 5) fit 48 teams in each pair arm, and it calls the exclusion timing unknown although the exclusion reason implies the 4 had already been paired.
